title: Pre-Clean – Effectiveness of Preoperative Antiseptic Skin Washing Prior to Standard Skin Disinfection in Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) – A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
This study investigates whether an additional antiseptic skin washing prior to the standard skin disinfection has an effect on the detection of microorganisms on the skin. In contrast to skin disinfection, antiseptic skin washing (pre-cleaning) involves a preliminary cleansing using an alcoholic solution and a soft cloth.

Participants are assigned to either the study group or the control group through a randomization process. Prior to the start of the study, the number of participants was determined with a 1:1 randomization ratio, meaning that the number of participants in the study group and the control group is equal.
Patients in the study group receive an additional antiseptic skin washing (pre-cleaning) before the standard hygiene procedures. Patients in the control group receive the standard skin disinfection, as recommended by current hygiene guidelines, immediately before surgery.
At specific time points, a skin swab is taken in the operating room using a sterile, soft swab within a designated area of approximately 25 cm².
The defined time points are as follows:
1. Before skin disinfection – control and study group
2. After antiseptic washing (pre-cleaning) – study group only
3. After standard skin disinfection – control and study group
The surface swabs collected are immediately sent to the microbiology laboratory for diagnostic analysis. The skin swabs are taken on the side of the affected hip, but not in the immediate area of the surgical incision.
Through these skin samples, we aim to determine whether and which microorganisms (the so-called skin flora) are present on your skin.
After three months, patients will be contacted for a brief telephone interview to answer a short questionnaire. This aims to collect information on periprosthetic infections and re-operations that may have occurred outside of the University Hospital Leipzig (UKL).

interventions.name: In patients assigned to the intervention group, three preoperative skin swabs are taken using a sterilized metal template with a window of 25 cm². The template area is swabbed using a sterile swab (eSwab™) by evenly dabbing horizontally and vertically. The template is positioned on the lateral thigh

In patients from the control group, two skin swabs are taken. The first swab is performed before the standard skin antisepsis with PI (Sample A), and the second swab is taken after the antisepsis has dried (Sample C). Additionally, a sham sample (Sample B) is collected to achieve single blinding.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
patients undergoing elective total hip arthroplasty at the University Hospital Leipzig
Exclusion criteria:
prior hip surgery on the affected side,
pre-existing skin conditions or infections in the hip area,
known allergy to any of the antiseptics used (e.g., iodine allergy),
antibiotic therapy within the past 12 weeks,
inability to provide informed consent for participation in the study.
